subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy, PII handling, logging & retention

Subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy, PII handling, logging & retention

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the pragmatic discussion. Below is a brief recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of pain points
- PII ingestion: must ensure sensitive customer data (names, SSNs, account numbers) is never persisted in cleartext outside your VPC.
- Audit & retention: compliance requires immutable audit logging for access events (retention target ~7 years) and the ability to export logs for e-discovery.
- Redaction: you need deterministic redaction at ingestion for specific fields and the option to apply additional redaction rules post-hoc.
- Embeddings / telemetry: must be able to disable telemetry and disable storing embeddings or derived artifacts that could contain PII.

Current stack you shared
- AWS (VPC), internal S3 buckets, Okta SSO, Datadog for observability; some inference currently runs on an internal ML infra.

Success criteria for pilot
1) PII never leaves FinServe cleartext: customer-managed KMS + Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) option.
2) Auditability: immutable, tamper-evident logs with export to your S3 and 7-year retention support.
3) Redaction and policy enforcement: configurable redaction rules (ingest + runtime).
4) Risk controls: ability to run a security assessment and ship SOC 2 evidence for vendor risk team.

What Redwood can provide (high level)
- Private deployment option (VPC) and on-prem packaging; support for customer-managed KMS/HSM.
- Configurable logging: audit events (who/what/when) are recorded and can be exported to your S3; retention is configurable and we support long-term retention policies.
- Built-in redaction hooks at ingestion + support for custom redaction plugins; option to disable model telemetry/embeddings storage per-tenant.
- SOC 2 Type II attestation and architecture diagram (attached).

Next steps
- I will share: SOC2_attestation_redwood_2026.pdf and redwood-arch-diagram.pdf (attached).
- Schedule a technical security call: propose Wed 12/3 @ 10am PT with your security eng + our infra/security leads (Rishi + Vivek). Please confirm availability.
- If you want, we can prepare a short pilot agreement and a mutual action plan to align milestones and the procurement timeline.

Attachments: SOC2_attestation_redwood_2026.pdf; redwood-arch-diagram.pdf

Thanks — let me know if I missed anything.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finserve.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Data privacy, PII handling, logging & retention

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we loop in security:  

1) Private deployment: does that mean we can run the inference runtime entirely inside our VPC with zero egress? We need to be explicit that no model artifacts or customer-derived embeddings are transmitted to Redwood-managed storage unless we opt in.
2) KMS: can you confirm support for AWS KMS CMKs and HSM-backed keys? We require customer-managed keys for all encryption at rest.
3) Audit log format: our tooling ingests logs in JSON with specific fields. Can you push logs to our S3 prefix in that format (we can share the spec)?
4) Retention: 7 years is our target for audit logs; are you able to guarantee retention (we'll include this in our vendor risk doc)?

Timeline: procurement wants a short vendor pack this week (SOC2, contact for security, sample MSA).

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Cloud Security | FinServe Inc.

Hi Alex — great questions. Answers inline below.

1) Private deployment / zero egress: yes — we offer a Private (VPC) deployment where the inference runtime runs in your VPC. By default, customer data (requests/responses, embeddings) does not leave your environment unless you explicitly enable a managed-storage feature. We can provide network diagrams and a deployment checklist for your security team.

2) KMS/HSM: we support AWS KMS with customer-managed CMKs and integrations with external HSMs where required. Keys remain under your control.

3) Audit logs: we can stream audit events to your S3 in JSON. We have a configurable schema but can map to your spec — please send the spec and our infra team will confirm field mappings.

4) Retention guarantee: we support configurable retention policies and can export logs to your archived S3 with lifecycle policies you control. For formal contractual guarantees (e.g., 7-year retention & immutability), we can include language in the vendor contract/MSA and enable write-once storage solutions as part of the pilot scope.

Attached: SOC2_attestation_redwood_2026.pdf; I also uploaded a more detailed architecture diagram to the shared folder (link: https://redwood.app/hubspot/deal/FS-2026-0912).

Next steps (proposed)
- Technical security call: Wed 12/3 @ 10am PT — Rishi (infra/security) and Vivek (prod infra) will join.
- Share FinServe's log JSON spec and any mandatory vendor contract clauses you require.
- I'll work with Rishi to assemble a concise vendor pack (SOC2 + contact + sample MSA) for procurement.

If that works, I'll send a calendar invite for 12/3.

Best,
Marissa
